candidates.title: Conrail tabs Wright as president and chief operating officer
candidates.excerpt: Conrail has named John Wright its new president and chief operating officer, bringing aboard a freight rail veteran with decades of operating and executive experience. Wright most recently served as general manager of Indiana Harbor Belt Railroad, a 600-employee switching and belt-line railroad based in Hammond, Ind. He succeeds Brian Gorton, who retired from the carrier headquartered in Mount Laurel, N.J., and co-owned by Norfolk Southern and CSX. Conrail has approximately 920 employees, and operates 1,200 track-miles in the northern New Jersey, southern New Jersey/Philadelphia, and Detroit. Wright began his railroad career in 1996 as a conductor for NS (NYSE: NSC) before moving into executive positions at CSX Transportation (NASDAQ: CSX). candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — Weekly U.S. rail traffic continues to run ahead of 2025 levels, although results for the week ending Oct. 31, 2026, were a bit more modest than prior weeks. The overall figure included 233,816 carloads, an increase of 3% over the same week in 2025, and 280,264 containers and trailers, up 3.9%. For the year to date, the U.S. volume of 22,115,264 carloads and intermodal units is an increase of 3.8% over the first 43 weeks of 2025. The 9,843,359 carloads are a gain of 2.7%, while the 12,271,905 intermodal units are an increase of 4.7%. North American volume for the week, as reported by nine U.S., Canadian, and Mexican railroads, was 715,620 carloads and intermodal units, up 4.3% from the corresponding week in 2025. candidates.title: Hapag-Lloyd announces export gate-in restrictions at APMT Valencia
candidates.excerpt: Hapag-Lloyd has announced temporary restrictions on export container deliveries at APM Terminals Valencia due to ongoing congestion at the Spanish terminal. Effective immediately, the export container acceptance window has been reduced from 14 days to nine days before a vessel’s estimated time of arrival. The restriction will remain in place until further notice. Under the temporary arrangement, APMT Valencia will only accept export containers during the nine-day window. Containers delivered earlier may be rejected, potentially leading to delays and additional transport or storage costs. Hapag-Lloyd has advised customers and hauliers to check the relevant vessel gate opening dates before arranging deliveries to the terminal. The carrier added that exceptions will not be available during the restriction period. Changes to vessel calls will also not be permitted solely to accommodate containers delivered outside the authorised gate-in window.

candidates.title: Brazilian builds boat from rubbish to collect more rubbish
candidates.excerpt: Brazilian builds boat from rubbish to collect more rubbish A former Brazilian ocean canoeing champion has taken recycling to a floating extreme, constructing a boat from 230 discarded plastic containers so he can collect even more rubbish from the sea. Marcos Arnhold spent two months building the unusual craft in Guaratuba, southern Brazil, using 125 two-litre plastic bottles, 105 five-litre disinfectant containers and a metal roof rack salvaged from an old Volkswagen Kombi. The homemade vessel is destined for Guaratuba Bay and its surrounding mangroves, where Arnhold plans to collect discarded rubbish for delivery to a municipal recycling centre. The former athlete, who won Brazil’s national ocean canoeing championship in 2002, told local newspaper JB Litoral that initial flotation and stability tests have exceeded expectations. candidates.excerpt: Global trade is growing. The capacity it needs doesn’t stop at the quay A container terminal can handle more cargo than ever before and still leave its customers waiting. Larger vessels and more efficient shipping networks have transformed how goods move across oceans. But the roads, railways and inland connections behind many ports have not kept pace. For much of the past 15 years, investment in landside infrastructure has lagged behind the changing demands of trade. That gap was easier to manage when there was room in the system. This year, geopolitical disruption, shifting trade routes and resilient cargo demand have exposed it. A port’s capacity and the capacity of the supply chain it serves are two different numbers.’’ The challenge looks different depending on where you stand. CN 3Q profit rises 6% as freight revenue climbs
candidates.excerpt: Canadian National Railway reported a 6% increase in third-quarter profit Friday as stronger grain, energy and automotive freight activity lifted revenue, while higher fuel costs and a technology write-down weighed on reported margins. The Montreal-based railway (NYSE: CNI) maintained its full-year earnings outlook, saying growth was tracking toward the upper end of its forecast range. CN earned C$1.209 billion ($866 million), or $1.43 per diluted share, in the three months ended Sept. 30, compared with $816 million, or $1.31 a share, a year earlier. Revenue increased 15% to $3.42 billion from $2.98 billion. Adjusted diluted earnings rose 18% to approximately $1.55 a share, excluding a software impairment and rail-merger-related advisory expenses. That exceeded analysts’ expectations of about $1.50 a share, according to FactSet figures reported by Dow Jones. Revenue also topped the approximately $3.34 billion forecast. candidates.title: Schneider to shift eastern rail business to Norfolk Southern from CSX
candidates.excerpt: Schneider will make Norfolk Southern its primary eastern rail provider under an agreement announced Oct. 29 aimed at expanding domestic intermodal capacity and giving shippers more options to move freight across the eastern United States. The agreement, effective in November, shifts Schneider’s NYSE: SNDR) company-owned equipment, drivers and logistics operations away from CSX (NASDAQ: CSX) and pairs it with Norfolk Southern’s 22-state intermodal network. The companies said the partnership would expand market access, increase capacity flexibility and help attract freight now moving by truck. “As we transition our primary eastern rail provider to Norfolk Southern, we’ll expand access to key markets, increase network flexibility and create new opportunities to better serve our customers,” said Michael Baumgardt, Schneider’s executive vice president of intermodal and logistics, in a release. Brian Kemp and Georgia Ports Authority officials celebrated the grand opening of the $134 million Gainesville Inland Port on Thursday, marking a new connection between Northeast Georgia’s manufacturing economy and international markets through the Port of Savannah. The ceremony followed the terminal’s operational opening on May 4.
